logline: A baby zombie is proud to be the littlest soldier in an army of seventy that waits in a dark room under its general's bed, until one morning a brother runs into the sunlight, a spider comes that night, and the general brings a new brother himself.
question: why tf are seventy zombies kept in a dark room under his bed?
premise: Seventy zombies stand in a dark room under a house in Ravenford, and have for two hundred nights. The narrator, the littlest (a baby zombie), is sure they're an army. Their general (a player, seen only from the knees down or as a silhouette in the hole) sleeps right on top of them, never goes far, and every night opens a hole in his yard and counts them. Up there the nights are always quiet: no monsters, just them. One morning he opens the hole in daylight; Brother Seventy runs to see him, into the sun, and burns. 'Sixty-nine.' That night a spider climbs the general's wall. The next night the general brings a new zombie and drops it down the hole himself. Nothing climbs the wall after that.
twist: They aren't an army. They're seventy ordinary un-named zombies kept within 32 blocks of the player's bed to fill his hostile mob cap: in Java 1.21 natural monster spawning near a player stops while 70 monsters that count toward his cap are near him (minecraft.wiki/w/Mob_spawning#Java_Edition_mob_cap, per player since 1.18). So no monster can spawn anywhere near him or the village. When one burned, the count fell to 69 and a spider spawned and came for him; he brings it back to seventy himself. 'Seventy.' Cut on the seventy faces turned up to him.
payoff_note: L15 is the reveal, said: 'When we're SEVENTY, no monster comes NEAR the general, but at sixty-NINE there was ROOM for one.' over S15 (the bare wall, the quiet village). Then the one beat: L16 the general's 'Seventy.' over S16; the lid goes back on, black, cut 1.0 s after the word. It loops into L01 ('Our general keeps SEVENTY of us...').
punch_note: hook L01 (fact + why), turn L08 (too sleepy to count), reveal L15 (at seventy no monster comes near him; at 69 there was room for one), sting L16 (the count back at seventy)

look.note: per shot (shots[].time): tonight's count before bed 13200 (S01, S02, S05, S06, S07, S16), then bed 13500 (S03); midday on the bench 6000 (S04); the sleepy night 12800 (S08, sleep skips to morning); the morning 1000 (S09-S12); the spider night 14000 (S13, awake); the next night 13600 (S14); a night after 13000 (S15). The room is dark (block light 0): every room shot is lit only by the hole (moon or sun) and the renderer's floor brightness (engine note).

world.canon: The general is Grandpa (Ravenford): `zuri` skin, the slow walk, seen only from the knees down or as a dark head in the hole, never named, never called Grandpa (conflict 11). His voice is his canon `elder` (Charon). He built the room about day 2000 (two hundred nights before), after Thirty-One Raids (1900): the tower hunts of that Short are before it. From day ~2000 Ravenford has no natural night monsters within 128 blocks of his bed while he's home (Red Sheep, 2300, shows none). Raids, patrols and the evoker are not stopped by it (never said). Who else sleeps in the house is not said; Buh is not shown and nobody says his name.

lines.text: Our general keeps SEVENTY of us / under his BED. / And I don't know WHY.
lines.say: Our general keeps seventy of us under his bed. And I don't know why.
lines.note: hook (story_format beat 1): the impossible, countable fact AND the why, said by 3 s; proud and bright, then a genuinely curious 'why' (the kid wants to know, never scared)

lines.text: I'm the LITTLEST SOLDIER. / He never takes us to FIGHT. / I think he's SAVING us / for something BIG.
lines.say: I'm the littlest soldier. He never takes us to fight. I think he's saving us for something big.
lines.note: proud, chin up (two-way clue: an army that never fights; misreading: saved for a big battle)

lines.text: Our GENERAL / SLEEPS / right ABOVE us.
lines.say: Our general sleeps right above us.
lines.note: admiring: guarding us all night (the misreading)

lines.text: He never goes FAR. / I think he'd MISS us.
lines.say: He never goes far. I think he'd miss us.
lines.note: sweet and sure of it (the misreading: he stays because he loves us)

lines.text: Every NIGHT / he opens the HOLE / and COUNTS us.
lines.say: Every night he opens the hole and counts us.

lines.direction: half to himself, unhurried; a tiny settle on the last number

lines.text: Always SEVENTY. / No new SOLDIERS ever come. / I think the world's / all FULL of us.
lines.say: Always seventy. No new soldiers ever come. I think the world's all full of us.
lines.note: proud and certain: the army is so big there's nobody left to join (two-way clue: the number never changes, nothing new comes; misreading of the full cap)

lines.text: Then one night / he was too SLEEPY / to COUNT us.
lines.say: Then one night he was too sleepy to count us.
lines.note: the turn: a little sad for him, sweet

lines.text: So he opened the HOLE / in the MORNING.
lines.say: So he opened the hole in the morning.
lines.note: happy: a morning visit, a treat, not a warning

lines.text: Brother SEVENTY / RAN to see him. / Right into the SUN.
lines.say: Brother Seventy ran to see him. Right into the sun.
lines.note: happy for him: he loves the general most

lines.text: He went all GLOWY. / Then he was GONE.
lines.say: He went all glowy. Then he was gone.
lines.note: puzzled, still light: a magic trick it doesn't get (the misreading of burning); not sad, not scared

lines.direction: flat and quiet, the count stopping short

lines.text: That NIGHT, / we HEARD a SPIDER / at the general's WINDOW. / The FIRST one ever. / I think it was LOOKING / for Brother SEVENTY.
lines.say: That night, we heard a spider at the general's window. The first one ever. I think it was looking for Brother Seventy.
lines.note: sweet and sure: a friend came to find him (the misreading); the general (the one the kid loves) is what it's climbing toward

lines.text: Next NIGHT, / the GENERAL brought / a new SOLDIER. / Right down the HOLE.
lines.say: Next night, the general brought a new soldier. Right down the hole.
lines.note: delighted: a new recruit for the army (the misreading)

lines.text: When we're SEVENTY, / no monster comes NEAR the general, / but at sixty-NINE / there was ROOM for one.
lines.say: When we're seventy, no monster comes near the general, but at sixty-nine there was room for one.
lines.note: THE REVEAL (story_format beat 6), one plain sentence: the kid, proud, thinking of room in the army, says what it noticed; it pays off L07's 'the world's all FULL of us'. The casual viewer makes the one jump: only so many monsters fit near him, and he fills every place. Proud, light on ROOM, no dread

lines.direction: quiet and satisfied, an old man to himself

have: zombie model, baby proportions (renderer/entities.js BABY / poseBaby), mob head pitch (B.head rotation from s.pitch; K.tp with pitch for NoAI mobs)
spider model with SpiderEyesLayer (eyes full bright: reads at night)
the on-fire overlay (fire_0/fire_1, EntityRenderDispatcher.renderFlame) for mobs, the death tip-over and red flash, the poof particles
our own sky/block light engine (renderer/light.js): sky light 15 straight down an open 1x1 shaft, so the daylight/moonlight square under the hole is drawn by the same rules as vanilla
block-break crack particles (the lid breaking), player actors with skins (zuri), held items (crossbow), name tags opt-in (`stunt.nameTags`): off by default, so the general has none
camera shots with at/look/fov; a red bed, bookshelf, composter, grass and stone as plain block models
missing: readability of a block-light-0 room lit only through a 1x1 shaft (S01, S02, S07, S09-S11, S16): not tested; the night grade may crush 70 green faces to black at 300 px. Needs a still test, maybe a per-shot shadow lift (no new light source)
70 zombies in one render: no story has drawn this many mobs at once; check the renderer's frame time and the recording's entity budget
a player head seen from straight below against the sky (the general's silhouette, head pitched 90 down over the shaft): pose and readability untested
a hard time cut inside one line (S11: burning, cut on 'Then' to the empty light ~20 s later): needs two set-ups joined in the edit at a word mark; check edit.py supports a cut mid-line
the ported palisade and east gate in map.json (still Thirty-One Raids' own build; Red Sheep needs the same port)
doMobLoot off for S11 only (a gamerule toggle in the stunt: kit, not renderer)
